dedupe_keys.name: nature based solutions in a school building at solana de los barros extremadura life mybuildingisgreen spain

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study describes how the LIFE project myBUILDINGisGREEN designed, built and monitored nature-based solutions on a primary school in Solana de los Barros, Badajoz, in Extremadura, Spain, where regional scenarios project average temperatures about 4 degrees C higher by the end of the century under a high emission scenario. The measures fall into four groups: several types of green roof, green facades, ventilation systems and permeable, greened outdoor areas, chosen with the school community to cut indoor temperatures and water use. A detailed monitoring scheme reported positive results, with savings in electricity and water, more local biodiversity and pollinator corridors, and native species to avoid invasive ones, and the partners worked to bring such measures into the Spanish building code. The pilot was selected in 2019 and built by 2021, with monitoring, dissemination and building code work expected to 2028. The page is free HTML on the Climate-ADAPT portal (2026), based on the project layman report and deliverables. Caveats: it is one building, detailed figures sit in project deliverables, and results are reported by the project. It illustrates design and retrofit testing of building-scale green infrastructure for heat and water scarcity; a related record is i-Tree.
name: Nature-based solutions in a school building at Solana de los Barros, Extremadura (LIFE myBUILDINGisGREEN, Spain)
outcomes: Monitoring of green roofs, facades and ventilation in the school reported lower energy and water use and biodiversity gains, supporting proposals to include nature-based solutions in the building code.
